messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The issue described in the bug report arises because the PosixParser incorrectly interprets a parameter value that begins with a hyphen ("-") as a new option parameter rather than as a value for the preceding option.

From the test:
- Options are built and a PosixParser is used.
- The argument list contains two tokens: "-t" and "-something".
- The test expects the parser to interpret "-something" as the parameter value for the option "-t".
- However, the parser treats "-something" as a new option, leading to faulty parsing.

The core parsing happens in Parser.parse() which processes tokens individually after they are flattened by flatten().

In PosixParser.flatten() method:
- Each token starting with "-" (excluding "--" special cases) is checked.
- If the token length is 2 and the options contain it, it is added directly as an option.
- Otherwise, if options.hasOption(token) is false, the token is "burst" into characters by burstToken() method.

In burstToken():
- For each character after the first in the token, it checks if that character is an option.
- If found, it adds the option and, if that option requires an argument, adds the remainder of the string as the argument.
- If not an option, depending on stopAtNonOption it either processes it or adds it with a hyphen prefix.

The problem is that the burstToken interprets the whole "-something" as multiple separate options, instead of treating "-something" as a single value string to the option "-t".

In other words, the logic assumes tokens longer than two characters and starting with '-' either match a complete option or should be split into single character options, whereas sometimes such tokens represent values with leading hyphens, which should not be split.

Hence, the parser misinterprets "-something" as a set of single-letter options, causing the reported problem.

The similar recent reports also mention issues around handling arguments with leading hyphens and property=value patterns, confirming that the core problem relates to token interpretation and flattening in the PosixParser.

# Suggested methods to address:
- PosixParser.flatten(Options, String[], boolean)
- PosixParser.burstToken(String, boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.flatten(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.burstToken(java.lang.String, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
